meta.note: Two kinds of entry are merged here: the machine-fault matrices (om-42 to om-44) and the weld-diagnosis pages (om-36 to om-41). Each cause is paired with its printed remedy and carries the page it came from. `applies_to` matters: several causes in the wire-welding tables are marked '(MIG only)' in the manual because flux-cored welding uses no shielding gas.

safety_preamble.text: Be CERTAIN to shut off the Welder, disconnect it from power, and discharge the MIG Gun to ground before adjusting, cleaning, or repairing the unit. Follow all safety precautions whenever diagnosing or servicing the equipment.

entries.symptom: Porosity in a MIG or flux-cored weld — small cavities or holes in the bead

causes.remedy: Check that polarity is set correctly for the type of welding. MIG (solid wire with gas) runs DCEP; self-shielded flux-cored runs DCEN.
Increase flow of gas. Clean nozzle. Maintain proper CTWD.
Use shielding gas recommended by the wire supplier.
Clean workpiece down to bare metal. Make certain that wire is clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.
Maintain steady travel speed.
Reduce CTWD (contact tip to work distance).
Check gas bottle and replenish as necessary.

causes.cause: Not enough or too much shielding gas
causes.remedy: Check gas regulator to ensure proper flow.
Clean workpiece down to bare metal.

entries.symptom: Porosity in a stick weld — small cavities or holes in the bead

causes.remedy: Clean workpiece down to bare metal. Make certain that fill material and Electrode are clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.
Maintain steady weld speed.

entries.symptom: Excessive spatter on a MIG or flux-cored weld

causes.remedy: Clean workpiece down to bare metal. Make certain that wire is clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.
Check that polarity is set correctly for type of welding.
Increase flow of gas. Clean nozzle. Maintain proper CTWD.
Reduce wire feed speed.
Reduce CTWD.

entries.symptom: Excessive spatter on a stick weld

causes.remedy: Clean workpiece down to bare metal. Make certain that fill material and Electrode are clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues. Note that fine spatter is normal; spatter that is grainy and large is a problem.

entries.symptom: Crooked or wavy bead on a MIG or flux-cored weld

causes.remedy: Use two hands or rest hand on steady surface.
Maintain steady travel speed.
Reduce CTWD.

entries.symptom: Crooked or wavy bead on a stick weld

causes.remedy: Use two hands or rest hand on steady surface.
Maintain steady weld speed.

entries.symptom: Burn-through on a MIG or flux-cored weld — base material melts away leaving a hole

causes.remedy: Reduce current and/or wire feed speed.
Increase travel speed and ensure that travel speed is kept steady.
Reduce wire feed speed.

entries.symptom: Burn-through on a stick weld — base material melts away leaving a hole

causes.remedy: Reduce current.
Increase welding speed and ensure that welding speed is kept steady.
Reduce amount of fill material.

entries.symptom: Wire feed motor runs but wire does not feed properly

causes.remedy: Increase wire feed pressure properly (step 27 on page 17).
Flip roll to correct size — see the Feed Roller instructions on page 12.

causes.cause: Damaged MIG Gun, cable, or liner assembly
causes.remedy: Have a qualified technician inspect these parts and replace as necessary.
Loosen Feed Tensioner so it applies only enough pressure to prevent continued spinning after the Gun Trigger is released.

entries.symptom: Wire creates a bird's nest during operation

causes.remedy: Adjust wire feed pressure properly (step 27 on page 17).
Replace with the proper tip for the wire used.

causes.cause: MIG Gun Cable Connector not fully inserted into Wire Feed mechanism
causes.remedy: Insert Gun Cable Connector properly (steps 13 and 14 on page 13).
Have a qualified technician inspect and repair/replace as necessary.

causes.cause: Gun cable is severely bent and the wire feed mechanism cannot feed wire
causes.remedy: Straighten Gun cable.

causes.cause: Gun liner is clogged or worn
causes.remedy: Check gun liner for obstruction. Replace if necessary.

causes.cause: Gun liner is too small for the welding wire being used
causes.remedy: Check that gun liner is the correct size for the wire.

causes.cause: Wire is tangled on the spool
causes.remedy: Check wire for cross winding or tangled spool.

causes.cause: Wire is not making contact with the feed rollers
causes.remedy: Check Feed Rollers and ensure the correct groove for the wire diameter is being used.

causes.cause: Feed roller is not making enough contact with the wire, or is crushing flux-cored wire
causes.remedy: Check Feed Tensioner and ensure it is set properly.
See the wire feed troubleshooting entries.

causes.cause: Incorrect Contact Tip or liner size, or excessive wear
causes.remedy: Replace with the proper tip or liner size for the wire used.
Adjust wire feed speed to achieve a more stable arc.

causes.cause: Loose MIG Gun cable or ground cable
causes.remedy: Check to ensure that all connections are tight.

causes.cause: Damaged MIG Gun or loose connection within the gun
causes.remedy: Have a qualified technician inspect and repair/replace as necessary.

causes.cause: Incorrect polarity for the process being run
causes.remedy: Ensure polarity is correct: DCEP for MIG welding and DCEN for flux-cored self-shielded welding.

causes.cause: Gas coverage insufficient or too high
causes.remedy: Ensure gas flow rate is set according to the Settings Chart. Make sure the MIG Gun Cable Connector is fully inserted into the wire feed mechanism with no O-rings exposed.
Check the ground clamp connection to the workpiece and machine. Ensure the MIG Gun is properly secured.
Check the line voltage and, if insufficient, have a licensed electrician remedy the situation.

causes.cause: Improper gauge or length of cord
causes.remedy: Do not use an extension cord on this Welder. Use only one of the supplied power cords or an identical replacement cord.
Switch current to the proper setting for the metal thickness.

entries.symptom: Welder does not function when switched on

causes.cause: See the troubleshooting table for supply and connection checks.
causes.remedy: Check the power connection and supply circuit.

causes.cause: Supply circuit does not meet requirements
causes.remedy: The welder must be plugged into a properly grounded, GFCI protected 120VAC (20 amp rated) or 240VAC receptacle that matches the plug, on a circuit equipped with delayed action-type circuit breaker or fuses.

entries.symptom: LCD display does not light when the welder is switched on

causes.cause: See the troubleshooting table for display and supply checks.
causes.remedy: Verify the power supply and connections; if the display still does not light, have a qualified technician inspect the unit.

entries.symptom: Wire feeds, but arc does not ignite

causes.cause: See the troubleshooting table for ground and polarity checks.
causes.remedy: Check the ground clamp connection to bare metal on the workpiece and confirm the polarity matches the process being run.

entries.symptom: Coat of slag over a stick weld

causes.cause: Normal — slag is a necessary part of a stick weld and shields the weld from impurities.
causes.remedy: Clean off the slag with the Chipping Hammer and Wire Brush after welding.
